:::{#exm-ellipse}
#### Points on an ellipse

Take the [ellipse](#def-ellipse) with foci $\vu = (-4, 0)$ and $\vv = (4, 0)$
and $s = 10$,
which is larger than $\norm{\vu - \vv} = 8$.
The [point](#def-real-coordinate-space) $\vx = (0, 3)$ is on it:

$$
\ba
\norm{\vx - \vu} + \norm{\vx - \vv}
&= \sqrt{(0 + 4)^2 + 3^2} + \sqrt{(0 - 4)^2 + 3^2}
&& \text{(@def-euclidean-distance)}
\\
&= \sqrt{25} + \sqrt{25}
&& \text{(square and add)}
\\
&= 10.
&& \text{(take the square roots and add)}
\ea
$$

So is $(5, 0)$,
whose distances to the foci are $9$ and $1$.
When the foci coincide, $\vu = \vv$,
both distances are $\norm{\vx - \vu}$,
so $2\norm{\vx - \vu} = s$.
Every point of the ellipse is therefore at distance $s / 2$ from $\vu$,
so the ellipse is the [circle](#def-circle) with center $\vu$ and radius $s / 2$.

:::{#fig-ellipse-example}

```{r}
#| label: ellipse-example-plot
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   An ellipse centered at the origin, 10 units wide and 6 units tall,
#|   drawn on equal axes. Hollow dots mark the foci (-4, 0) and (4, 0) on
#|   the horizontal axis. Solid dots mark the points (0, 3) and (5, 0) on
#|   the ellipse, and two dashed segments, each of length 5, join (0, 3) to
#|   the two foci.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 6
# With foci (-4, 0) and (4, 0) and s = 10, the ellipse reaches s / 2 = 5 along
# the axis through the foci and sqrt(5^2 - 4^2) = 3 across it.
angle <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 400)
ellipse <- tibble::tibble(
  x1 = 5 * cos(angle),
  x2 = 3 * sin(angle)
)
marks <- tibble::tribble(
  ~x1, ~x2, ~label, ~kind, ~nudge,
  -4, 0, "focus (-4, 0)", "focus", -0.6,
  4, 0, "focus (4, 0)", "focus", -0.6,
  0, 3, "(0, 3)", "on the ellipse", 0.6,
  5, 0, "(5, 0)", "on the ellipse", 0.6
)
to_foci <- tibble::tribble(
  ~x1, ~x2, ~x1_end, ~x2_end,
  0, 3, -4, 0,
  0, 3, 4, 0
)
shapes <- c(focus = 1, "on the ellipse" = 16)

ellipse |>
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::aes(x = x1, y = x2) +
  ggplot2::geom_path() +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    data = to_foci,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(xend = x1_end, yend = x2_end),
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = marks,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(shape = kind),
    size = 3
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = marks,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(y = x2 + nudge, label = label)
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = shapes, guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::coord_fixed() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "first coordinate", y = "second coordinate")
```

The [ellipse](#def-ellipse) with foci $(-4, 0)$ and $(4, 0)$ and $s = 10$.
The two dashed segments from $(0, 3)$ to the foci are each $5$ units long.
